html:
The Hill of Crosses near Šiauliai in northern Lithuania is a small hill covered with crosses, more than a hundred thousand of them, placed by pilgrims.

The first crosses were probably put up after the uprising against Russian rule in 1831, for rebels whose bodies were never found. Over time it became a place of prayer for Catholic Lithuanians. Under Soviet rule the authorities bulldozed it several times, but people came back at night to put up new crosses.

It became a symbol of the persistence of faith and of quiet resistance, as Catholicism was tied to Lithuanian identity since the late baptism of Lithuania. Pope John Paul II visited in 1993. See Lithuania and the Catholic Church.
sum: The Hill of Crosses near Šiauliai in northern Lithuania is a small hill covered with crosses, more than a hundred thousand of them, placed by pilgrims.
